questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to get to know British politics and culture better and was recommended University of York (UoY).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. The university reached out to me with information and held some online seminars where we could ask questions about everything pre-arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was picked up at the airport and taken to college I was staying at. There were some students to guide us to get our keys and stuff.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A big plus about UoY is that (at least for undergraduates) housing is guaranteed. There were both ensuite and shared bathroom options and different price ranges.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were both catered and non-catered options.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: York is expensive for housing and from what I've heard, it is very hard and expensive to get housing off-campus. There are a bunch of different colleges on campus with varying price levels. You can write your preferences in an email to the team, but there is no guarantee that you will get your first priority. However, the uni is very helpful – my first offer for accommodation was the opposite of what I had wanted, but I called them and got assigned a different room. So have faith in the process and do not hesitate to reach out to them, they are very kind and helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Finding the courses on offer was a bit difficult because not all modules are open for exchange students, so make sure to check that the modules you want are open for exchange students.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Depends on your department. For politics, they reached out via email around the beginning of September and asked which classes I would like to take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always email them or ask questions about it in the pre-arrival seminars.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient – the process might take place a lot later than at KU. However, within the first two weeks it is also possible to change classes, so if you do not get your preferred ones at first you might be able to get them then.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses vary a lot in difficulty. The first year course was very easy, but the second and third year couses were similar in level to KU. Maybe slightly fewer readings compared to KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar – 1 lecture and 1 seminar per class per week. During the lectures you mostly listen and take notes, and they are recorded and uploaded online which is very convenient. The seminars are very interactive and usually only around 10 people with a professor, so I learnt a lot during them.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POL00013C: Introduction to Comparative Politics (first year module)
POL00079I: European Union Politics (second year module)
POL00068H: Politics of Peace after Civil War (third year module)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Politics of Peace after Civil War was absolutely incredible – very interesting course materials and great professors! European Union Politics was taught by a quite fun professor, so if you're interested in the EU it is a good course, but it can be a bit heavy with the readings sometimes.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay a fee to join sports and societies. Sports were around 20-40 pounds I believe, while societies were only a couple of pounds.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Trains in the UK are expensive. However, grocery shopping is significantly cheaper than in Denmark, especially if you go to Aldi or Lidl.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many options, literally societies for every niche theme. Also loads of sports teams, music, theatre etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Whatever your heart desires honestly – joining societies and clubs is a great way to meet people. I did the choir, football and roller-blading and would recommend all three.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
York is such a lovely city, so make sure to make time to explore it! Go see the Minster (free for students at UoY), walk along the rivers and visit some cute cafés. York is also the UK's most haunted city, so go for a ghost tour if you're into that. For pubs, go to the Phoenix for jazz-night and the golden ball for folk music.

York is also a great location for exploring the UK – around 2 hours to London and 2,5 hours to Edinburgh via train. For nearby day-trips I would recommend Leeds, Whitby (very cheap with the bus and so pretty), Knaresborough and Newcastle.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, culturally the UK is quite similar to Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs, societies etc! And go to the international socializers in the first week.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Locals are generally pretty welcoming and open, especially in the Northern parts of the UK.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient with the application process, join societies/sports and explore the UK!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and experiencing a different university life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being ill and dealing with the NHS – they're were not very helpful and I had be quite insistent in order to see a doctor at the local GP.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
